title: Acid-catalysed enolisation of acetone
subtitle: Acid turns the ketone into its enol, one proton at a time

reactants.caption: acetone + H₃O⁺ (Cl⁻ is a spectator)
reactants.learnerPrompt: Acid catalysis starts at the carbonyl group. Protonate the ketone.
hintTiers: Which atom of acetone carries lone pairs and is the most basic site?
The carbonyl oxygen takes a proton from H₃O⁺. Two arrows: one makes the new O–H bond, one breaks the old one.
Carbonyl oxygen lone pair → the hydrogen of H₃O⁺; that O–H bond of H₃O⁺ → a lone pair on its oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: The α-hydrogen of a neutral ketone is not acidic enough for water to take it. Protonate the carbonyl oxygen first: the C=O⁺–H group pulls much harder on the α-C–H electrons.
H₃O⁺ is the acid here: it gives a proton. It does not add to carbon. Which atom of acetone can take the proton?

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right start: the carbonyl oxygen takes the proton. The hydrogen now has two bonds: break its bond to the oxygen of H₃O⁺ as well.

protonated-ketone.caption: protonated acetone + water
protonated-ketone.learnerPrompt: Water is the base now. Make the enol.
hintTiers: Protonating the oxygen makes the α-C–H much more acidic. Which C–H is next to the C=O⁺–H group?
Water takes the drawn α-hydrogen. The C–H electrons form a C=C bond, and the C=O π electrons move onto the positive oxygen. Three arrows.
Water lone pair → the drawn α-hydrogen; that C–H bond → a π bond to the carbonyl carbon; the C=O π bond → a lone pair on the carbonyl oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Water can add to the carbonyl carbon, but that gives the hydrate, a reversible dead end. Here water acts as a base on the α-hydrogen.
Taking the proton off oxygen just goes back to acetone. Remove a proton from the α-carbon instead.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Good: water takes the α-hydrogen and a C=C forms. The carbonyl carbon now has five bonds: move the C=O π electrons onto the oxygen.

steps.explanationAfterStep: The protonated ketone is an oxocarbenium ion. The positive oxygen pulls electron density out of the C=O bond and, through it, out of the α-C–H bond.
A C–H bond breaks and an O–H bond has formed: the enol is a tautomer of acetone, a different molecule, not a resonance form. H₃O⁺ is given back, so the acid is a catalyst.

mechanismSummary: Acid protonates the carbonyl oxygen. Water then removes a proton from the α-carbon, and the C=O π electrons move onto the oxygen, which keeps its proton: the enol. Overall a hydrogen has moved from carbon to oxygen. For acetone the enol is a tiny fraction at equilibrium (about 1 in 10⁸), but it forms fast in acid and is the nucleophile in acid-catalysed α-substitution.
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 20
